newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 27.

text.p: DDI Corp plans to purchase about 20 percent of undersea fiber-optic cables to be laid around Japan by Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd (KDD). It will pay KDD about 40 billion to 50 billion yen. The move will enable DDI to meet surging demand for circuits as well as put it in position to enter the international phone business. KDD is to start laying undersea fiber-optic cables in the second half of next year, and is due to complete them in early 1999.

Itochu Corp plans to start selling life insurance from April 1997. It will set up a sales company with a venture company in January, and conclude agency agreements with about 30 companies, including medium-sized life insurance firms and life insurance subsidiaries of non-life insurance firms. The company, capitalised at 20 million yen, will be owned 60 percent by Tokyo-based life-insurance agent Global Insurance and 40 percent by Itochu and its group companies.

Autoparts makers affiliated with Honda Motor Co Ltd plan to set up manufacturing bases in India to supply local production planned there by Honda as early as next year. Yutaka Giken Co Ltd, a press components maker, will launch a joint company with a local firm in February. The joint firm will produce 30,000 exhaust components annually from spring 1998. Toyota Motor Corp is also considering autoparts production in India.

Six leading Japanese home appliance retailers are expected to see current profits rise more than 10 percent in the business year to next March, helped by robust sales of personal computers, communications equipment and air conditioners. Kojima Co Ltd forecasts its sales will rise 24 percent to 280 billion yen and pretax profit will grow 11 percent to 7.4 billion yen. Joshin Denki Co Ltd, which sees pretax profit rising 27 percent to six billion yen, will raise dividend payments for the business year to March by two yen.
